purpose: Conversion factors for translating kg CO2e into human-scale equivalents. Every factor is sourced; provenance is in this file so that the blog post never displays an equivalent without being able to link to its origin.

equivalents.name: Quarter-pound beef burger
equivalents.concrete_reference: Equivalent to a McDonald's Quarter Pounder with Cheese or a Burger King Whopper Jr. (by beef mass)
equivalents.unit_description: One quarter-pound burger — 113 g cooked patty (from ~150 g raw beef), with bun, cheese, condiments
equivalents.range_reason: LCA estimates vary by ~3× depending on cattle system (feedlot vs pasture), region, and what's included (bun, cheese, transport). 6 kg is the midpoint of commonly cited values.

primary_source.title: Reducing food's environmental impacts through producers and consumers
primary_source.key_finding: Median 60 kg CO2e per kg beef (global LCA across 38,700 farms)

additional_sources.title: Climate change food calculator
additional_sources.key_finding: 1 beef burger (~150g cooked from 250g raw) = ~3.0 kg CO2e

additional_sources.title: Environmental Impacts of Food Production
additional_sources.key_finding: Cites Poore & Nemecek; provides per-100g and per-burger conversions

equivalents.methodology_notes: Source Library uses 6 kg CO2e per burger as the central. This captures the raw beef LCA (15 kg/kg × 0.25 kg = 3.75 kg) plus bun, cheese, cooking, and waste. The 3-8 kg range covers nearly all defensible LCA results.

equivalents.name: Average European petrol car, per km
equivalents.concrete_reference: EU passenger-car fleet average in 2024 — roughly a mid-size petrol hatchback like a VW Golf, Renault Clio, or Toyota Corolla (real-world fuel use, well-to-wheel emissions including fuel production). An EV on the average European grid would be ~60-100 g/km.
equivalents.unit_description: One kilometre driven by an average petrol passenger car in the EU fleet (well-to-wheel)
equivalents.range_reason: New cars hit ~110 g CO2/km tank-to-wheel (WLTP); fleet average for in-use cars is ~165-200 g CO2/km well-to-wheel including fuel production. 180 g/km is the central figure for EU fleet average in 2024.

primary_source.title: CO₂ performance of new passenger cars in Europe (2024 reporting cycle)
primary_source.key_finding: New EU cars average 108 g CO2/km (WLTP, manufacturer-declared). Real-world tank-to-wheel ~125 g/km. Well-to-wheel including fuel ~165-200 g/km depending on fuel mix.

additional_sources.title: Average CO2 emissions per km from new passenger cars

equivalents.methodology_notes: 180 g CO2/km used as central. This is the in-use fleet average for passenger petrol cars in Europe, well-to-wheel. EVs would be much lower (60-120 g/km depending on grid).

equivalents.name: AMS ↔ LHR round-trip flight (economy)
equivalents.concrete_reference: One passenger, economy seat, Amsterdam Schiphol to London Heathrow and back. Short-haul flight (~370 km each way), heavily emission-loaded per km due to takeoff/landing energy.
equivalents.unit_description: One passenger, economy class, round-trip Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS) to London Heathrow (LHR), with radiative forcing factor included
equivalents.range_reason: Short-haul flight emissions are dominated by takeoff/landing. Without radiative forcing factor (RFI) the number is ~130 kg; with RFI ≈ 1.9 (commonly used multiplier for high-altitude effects) it rises to ~245 kg. ICAO's methodology omits RFI; atmosfair and DEFRA include it.

primary_source.title: atmosfair flight calculator
primary_source.key_finding: AMS → LHR economy one-way ≈ 123 kg CO2e (RFI included). RT ≈ 245 kg.

additional_sources.title: UK government GHG conversion factors 2024
additional_sources.key_finding: Short-haul economy class: 0.158 kg CO2e per passenger-km (with RFI). AMS-LHR ~370 km × 2 × 0.158 ≈ 117 kg RT without RFI; 245 kg with.

additional_sources.title: ICAO Carbon Emissions Calculator
additional_sources.key_finding: Excludes RFI. AMS-LHR RT ≈ 110-130 kg CO2e.

equivalents.methodology_notes: Central 245 kg uses atmosfair (with RFI ≈ 1.9). Range 130-310 covers ICAO low (no RFI) to atmosfair high (premium economy / business adjustments).

equivalents.name: AMS ↔ NYC round-trip flight (economy)
equivalents.concrete_reference: One passenger, economy seat, Amsterdam to New York JFK and back. Long-haul (~5,860 km each way), more efficient per km than short-haul but the distance dominates.
equivalents.unit_description: One passenger, economy class, round-trip Amsterdam (AMS) to New York JFK, with radiative forcing factor included
equivalents.range_reason: Long-haul flights are more efficient per km than short-haul, but the distance is much larger. ~5,860 km one-way × 2 × 0.149 kg/passenger-km (long-haul economy DEFRA) × ~1.9 RFI ≈ 3,320 kg. Without RFI ~1,750 kg.

primary_source.title: atmosfair flight calculator
primary_source.key_finding: AMS → JFK economy one-way ≈ 1,475 kg CO2e (RFI included). RT ≈ 2,950 kg.

additional_sources.title: UK government GHG conversion factors 2024
additional_sources.key_finding: Long-haul economy: 0.149 kg CO2e per passenger-km (with RFI). AMS-JFK ~5,860 km × 2 × 0.149 ≈ 1,746 kg RT without RFI; ~3,320 kg with.

equivalents.methodology_notes: Central 2,950 kg uses atmosfair (with RFI ≈ 1.9). Business/first class would be 2-3× higher.

global_methodology_notes: All flight numbers include Radiative Forcing Index (RFI) at ≈1.9× the direct CO2 emissions. RFI captures non-CO2 climate impacts at altitude (NOx, contrails, water vapor). ICAO's official methodology excludes RFI; atmosfair and DEFRA include it. We use the with-RFI numbers because peer-reviewed climate science supports it, and most public-facing carbon offset calculators use it.
All numbers are 'per unit' — one burger, one km, one round-trip ticket per passenger.
Uncertainty ranges given are LCA-defensible bounds. Burgers vary most (factor ~3) due to cattle system differences; flights vary mainly by RFI inclusion (factor ~2).
We deliberately exclude offsets, carbon credits, or 'net' figures. All emissions are gross.
how_to_use: When displaying a CO2 number X kg in the blog, divide X by each equivalent's kg_co2e_per_unit to get the count. Show the range (X / high_range to X / low_range) where space allows. Always provide an inline citation [n] to this provenance file.
